styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow, tall white and grey appliance rack. Only 15 distinct colours cover the whole piece, against 38-40 for the stall and well references. Each material ramp (white casing, grey panels, dark interior) has about 3-4 steps, where Beodeul uses 5-6. The measured facts are acceptable: 12 visible tones per tile (hedge 9, stall 17, well 20), 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted. By eye, though, the dark blue-grey outline runs evenly around the whole silhouette, which gives a clean sticker look. The flat casing surfaces have little grain, speckle or per-part highlight, so it reads thinner and flatter than the stall and well. A careful artist would not accept it next to those references without more shading steps and surface texture.
